file_roles.evidence: eraseCursorGlobalIfAuthorized takes `const long long* ids` now; signature adaptation plus line wrapping.
Header declaration changed to `const long long* ids`; adaptation to new getArray() return type.
New bounds-checked DbMessage: ns read with strnlen limit and uassert 18633, checkRead<T> uassert 18634 'Not enough data to read' on every read; replaces unchecked reads.
Removes inline unchecked accessors (pullInt via raw pointer, getInt, getInt64, getOID, afterNS using strlen) and replaces them with checked methods.
receivedKillCursors read n and a long long array via raw `x++` pointer arithmetic with no length check; diff uses dbmessage.pullInt() and getArray(n) with checks; ns read goes through DbMessage.
gotKillCursors read cursor ids by casting message data with no size check; diff adds `massert(18632, bad kill cursors size ...)` and uses dbmessage.getArray(n).
Removes verify(_d.getns()) and uses _d.messageShouldHaveNs() in reset(); adaptation to the new DbMessage API.
Uses d.pullInt() and by-value pullInt64() in place of raw casts; API adaptation.
MsgData becomes a class with `_data` private and friend access; blocks direct raw access to message bytes, hardening without being the parse logic.

rationale: The report has no code, only that a crafted message can leak heap memory. The diff shows several message-parsing sites reading past the buffer without length checks (DbMessage, receivedKillCursors, gotKillCursors), and these are replaced with bounds-checked reads. Other files adapt to the new API.
notes: Issue text gives no location, so symptom location is inferred from the diff.
